DPDP Act (India) Statutory Rights

Privacy Rights & Data Erasure Portal

Statutory Reference: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Section 11 & Section 12)

Under India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, every homebuyer and prospective customer (Data Principal) possesses non-negotiable statutory rights over their personal information.

1. Right to Erasure & Consent Withdrawal (Section 12 & Section 6(4))

You may demand the immediate erasure of your personal data from RealSalePro's databases and active marketing campaigns at any time. When you submit an erasure request:

  • Your mobile number is immediately masked and anonymized across lead records.
  • All automated WhatsApp, SMS, and email follow-up communications cease instantly.
  • A permanent, cryptographically verifiable proof of erasure is written to our 3-year WORM compliance ledger.

2. WhatsApp Self-Service Opt-Out

For zero-friction privacy, you can withdraw consent simply by replying STOP, UNSUBSCRIBE, or DELETE MY DATA to any WhatsApp message sent from RealSalePro or our client developers.

3. Data Protection & Grievance Redressal Officer

In compliance with Rule 3(2) of the DPDP Rules, 2026, you may reach our designated Data Protection Officer directly:

  • Officer Name: Anuj Kumar Singh
  • Email Desk: grievance@realsalepro.com
  • Resolution Turnaround SLA: Within 72 working hours
  • Appellate Authority: Data Protection Board of India (DPDP Act Section 13(3))
